newsitem.title: RUSSIA: List of Russia's unsolved contract killings.
newsitem.headline: List of Russia's unsolved contract killings.

text.p: The brutal bomb attack on mourners at a Moscow cemetery on Sunday, which killed 13 people was the most violent in a long series of unsolved murders in Russia over the past five years.
In May officials said the number of murders in Russia doubled in 1995 to 31,000. Most of these were domestic killings, including thousands of women murdered by their partners.
Out of the total, 560 were defined as contract killings but only 60 were solved. Nearly half of the victims were businessmen and bankers while nearly 40 percent were criminal chiefs.
Of the murders that were solved, two out of three were carried out by bodyguards.
Among the best known unsolved murders since 1994 are the following:
April 26, 1994 - Duma deputy Andrei Azderdzis shot dead in his apartment building in Moscow suburb of Khimki
October 17, 1994 - Journalist Dmitry Kholodov of Moskovsky Komsomolets newspaper blown up in his office by a booby-trapped briefcase after investigating military corruption
March 1, 1995 - Popular TV journalist Vladislav Listyev shot dead outside his apartment building. His murder is linked to control of lucrative TV advertising market
August 4, 1995 - Ivan Kivelidi, chairman of Russian Business Round Table, was murdered by poisoning
June 12, 1996 - Viktor Mosalov, mayor of Zhukovsky near Moscow, killed
October 1, 1996 - South Korean diplomat Choi Duck-keun bludgeoned to death outside his apartment in Vladivostok

November 3, 1996 - U.S. businessman Paul Tatum, locked in a business dispute with Russian partners over ownership of a luxury hotel, killed by a volley of automatic weapon fire as he enters Moscow's Kievskaya metro station.
